title: Forensics Evidence Handback Procedure (Appendix)
content:
Purpose:
This appendix defines a consistent, legally defensible procedure for exchanging, packaging, and returning forensic artifacts to customers, auditors, or law enforcement in the context of Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments. It is intended to supplement contractual obligations (DPAs, SLAs, MSA exhibits) with operational requirements, minimal disclosure principles, and a clear chain-of-custody model.

Scope:
Applies to: Redwood-hosted artifacts created or collected during incident response, live forensics captures on private deployments (VPC/air-gapped), ephemeral KV/prefix caches, runtime logs, metadata snapshots, and any customer-owned data derived from inference sessions that may be requested for legal or compliance purposes. Not intended for bulk data export requests that are governed by Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) procedures; however, overlap and coordination should be handled by Security & Privacy.

Key principles:
- Minimize: return only the smallest set of artifacts necessary to satisfy the request or legal obligation.
- Verifiable integrity: every artifact handed back must include a cryptographic hash and a recorded custody chain.
- Time-bounded access: evidence handback windows should be explicitly limited and auditable.
- Customer control: where feasible, customers choose extraction scope and redaction levels; Redwood provides templates and recommended defaults.

Definitions (short):
- Artifact: discrete data export (log segment, KV snapshot, model input bundle, memory dump).
- Custody record: sequential log entries documenting access, transfer, and recipients for an artifact.
- Evidence package: signed bundle of artifacts, metadata, and custody record delivered to requester.

Request intake and validation:
1) Intake channel: All evidence requests must be opened in the SECOPS intake queue (Jira SECOPS or SecOps intake form). Requests received via sales, legal, or customer success should be forwarded to SECOPS within 4 business hours.
2) Request classification: SECOPS triages to one of three classes: Operational (customer-led troubleshooting), Legal/Third-party (subpoena, law enforcement), or Audit/Compliance (customer auditor or certification body). Classification must be documented in the intake ticket.
3) Authorization: For Operational requests, customer account owner + Security lead approval required. For Legal/Third-party, Security lead + Legal counsel sign-off required. For Audit/Compliance, Security + Customer Success agreement required.

Scope determination and minimization checklist:
- Identify minimal time range and service component (model route, deployment zone, node id).
- Prefer metadata extracts over raw payloads when practicable (e.g., hashed probe IDs, truncated prompts).
- Evaluate need for KV cache / memory dumps only if reproducing the incident otherwise impossible.
- Track rationale for any full memory or model weight snapshot capture in the intake ticket.

Artifact collection standards:
- Collection agents: use approved collection tooling (forensics-agent v2) that preserves timestamps, user IDs, and collection operator identity. Manual downloads (ssh/scp) are allowed only if automated tooling cannot access the target; manual flows require two operators and video/time-stamped evidence of the operation.
- Integrity: generate SHA-256 hashes at point of capture and again after packaging. Record hash values in custody records.
- Metadata: each artifact must include a metadata header with origin (service, region, node), capture window, rationale, operator id, and ticket id.

Packaging and delivery formats:
- Preferred format: signed ZIP with directory layout:
  /evidence/<ticket-id>/artifacts/<artifact-name>
  /evidence/<ticket-id>/metadata/<artifact-name>.json
  /evidence/<ticket-id>/custody-record.log
- Each package must include a signed manifest.json listing artifacts, SHA-256 hashes, collection timestamps, and operator signatures (GPG or Redwood KMS-signed JWT).
- Delivery channels: secure file transfer (SFTP with customer public key), encrypted cloud share (pre-signed URL valid 7 days, recommended only for low-sensitivity material), or physical delivery on encrypted media for extremely sensitive cases (requires legal sign-off).

Chain of custody and access logging:
- Custody record entries must be append-only and stored in SECOPS audit store with retention >= 7 years (unless otherwise contractually limited).
- Each custody entry: timestamp, operator, action type (capture, package, transfer), artifact id, pre/post-hash, destination, and authorization reference.
- For any handback, provide a custody timeline and an access digest to the customer.

Redaction and pseudonymization guidance:
- Default approach: prefer pseudonymization over redaction when preserving forensic value. Use consistent reversible tokenization when the customer permits; keys remain customer-controlled if operating in Private deployments.
- Redaction rules must be documented and reversible only under court order or customer consent. Record redaction rationale in the manifest.

Retention, deletion, and proof-of-deletion:
- Temporary artifacts created for a specific handback shall be retained only for the minimal operational period (standard: 90 days) unless the customer or legal hold extends this.
- Proof of deletion: when artifacts are deleted, produce a signed deletion statement containing artifact id, final hash, deletion method, operator id, and deletion timestamp. Record the statement in the ticket and send to the customer.

SLA and timing expectations:
- Intake acknowledgement: 4 business hours.
- Scope determination and authorization: 3 business days for Operational; 7 business days for Legal/Third-party (longer for complex requests).
- Initial artifact delivery (where feasible): 10 business days from authorization. Delays must be logged and communicated with reasons.

Customer and Redwood responsibilities:
Customer responsibilities:
- Supply precise scope, business justification, and required retention windows.
- Provide public keys or secure endpoints for delivery.
- Approve redaction/pseudonymization defaults or accept suggested defaults.

Redwood responsibilities:
- Use approved tooling and trains operators in chain-of-custody protocols.
- Keep detailed custody records and enable reproducible verification of artifact integrity.
- Escalate to Legal for any third-party or ambiguous requests.

Special cases: law enforcement requests and subpoenas:
- Do not produce artifacts in response to informal law enforcement requests. All such requests must be forwarded to Redwood Legal immediately.
- Redwood Legal will seek to narrow scope and, where permitted, provide a redacted package or preservation notice. Custody and notification obligations to customers depend on contract and local law; all actions documented in the ticket.

Audit and attestation:
- Periodic audits: security will perform tabletop tests and 12-month process audits of random evidence handback tickets to validate compliance. Findings will be summarized for the InfoSec steering committee.
- Customer attestation: when requested by the customer, provide a summary statement of process compliance rather than raw custody data unless contractually required.

Example minimal timeline (Operational request):
- Day 0: Customer opens SECOPS intake form. Ticket created. Acknowledgement within 4 hours.
- Day 1: Triage and scope agreed with customer. Authorization recorded.
- Day 2–4: Artifact collection using forensics-agent v2. SHA-256 hashes recorded.
- Day 5: Packaging, manifest creation, and internal review.
- Day 6: Delivery via SFTP and customer confirmation of receipt.

Sign-off and escalation matrix:
- Security Lead (Priya Nair): final operational sign-off for Operational requests.
- General Counsel: required for Law Enforcement, subpoenas, or requests involving cross-border transfer.
- VP Customer Success: required where handback might materially impact customer SLAs or service continuity.

Appendices (references):
- Artifact schema: github:infra/forensics-schemas#artifact-v1 (includes metadata fields and example JSON).
- SECOPS intake form: confluence:SEC-Incident-Intake-Form.
- Forensics tooling SOP: confluence:Forensics-Agent-SOP-v2.

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Default retention window for ephemeral inference caches in Dedicated deployments (proposal: 30 days unless otherwise contracted).
- Whether to enable customer-managed encryption keys by default for evidence packages in Private deployments.

Revision history:
- 2024-10-18: Draft authored by Priya Nair.
- 2024-11-12: Added packaging manifest requirements (Maya Chen).
- 2025-02-14: Incorporated Legal feedback on law enforcement escalation (Diego Alvarez).
